# BPUT Hackathon 2026 — PS05 Final Technical Report

## GPS-Denied 3D Autonomous UAV with LiDAR–Camera Fusion, 3D Planning and Precision Landing

*Generated by `scripts/generate_report.py` from logged simulation data (repository revision ``). Every number in sections 28–34 is read from `results/`; anything not measured is marked NOT MEASURED.*

## 2. Abstract
A simulated 5–7 kg-class quadrotor (PX4 X500 airframe) flies a 50 m × 50 m 3D obstacle course without GPS. Position comes from the PS05 external tracking station (r, θ, φ) fused by PX4 EKF2; a forward RGB camera and a 360° 3D LiDAR are time-synchronised and fused into an RGB point cloud that builds a ray-traced 3D occupancy map. A weighted 3D A* plans inside an approved mission corridor around inflated obstacles; a local layer stops and replans when new obstacles appear on the path. A downward camera detects an AprilTag and a downward flash LiDAR validates the landing surface before and during a staged precision descent. Across 5 logged simulation trials the horizontal landing error over all landed runs was mean 3.3 cm, RMSE 3.5 cm, P95 5.3 cm (n = 5), with 0 collisions.

## 3. Problem statement
PS05 requires GPS-independent autonomous guidance of a UAV in a 3D environment: determine the vehicle state without satellite positioning, keep it inside a permissible corridor around an approved trajectory (E = √(ΔX²+ΔY²+ΔZ²) ≤ Emax, otherwise critical alarm and containment), and — per the implementation guides — perceive obstacles with LiDAR and camera, plan and replan in 3D, and land precisely on a marked pad after validating it.

## 4. Motivation
GNSS is unreliable in urban canyons, under canopy and under jamming/spoofing. A 5–7 kg UAV failing over people is hazardous, so the system must be predictable (approved corridor), able to react to the unexpected (perception + replanning) and conservative at touchdown (independent geometric validation).

## 5. Requirements
Derived from the three supplied PS05 documents; the full requirement-by-requirement matrix with evidence is `docs/REQUIREMENTS_TRACEABILITY.md`. Key quantitative targets: no GPS in the guidance chain; tracking latency < 20 ms; telemetry > 50 Hz; mean simulated trajectory error E < 0.5 m; landing error, success rate, clearance, latencies and collisions reported over 20–30+ trials.

## 6. System architecture
Gazebo Harmonic simulates world, physics and sensors; PX4 v1.17.0 SITL is the flight controller; ROS 2 Jazzy carries all perception, mapping, planning and landing logic; the web dashboard is a read-only observer. Data flow and package map: `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, ROS graph: `docs/ROS_GRAPH.md`.

## 7. PX4 architecture
PX4 runs in lockstep with Gazebo (standalone gz mode). Custom airframe `4050_gz_x500_ps05`: `EKF2_GPS_CTRL=0`, `EKF2_EV_CTRL=3`, `EKF2_HGT_REF=3` (external vision), `UXRCE_DDS_SYNCT=0` (sim time), offboard-loss → LAND. `px4_interface` is the only node talking to PX4 (OffboardControlMode heartbeat, TrajectorySetpoint, VehicleCommand over uXRCE-DDS); if the autonomy stops sending setpoints the heartbeat stops and PX4's own failsafe takes over.

## 8. Gazebo architecture
World and vehicle are generated from YAML (`scripts/generate_world.py`, `generate_vehicle_model.py`): buildings, a long wall, poles, trees, an overhead canopy, a box cluster, guarded landing pad with a 0.40 m AprilTag 36h11, a tracking-station mast and three movable scenario objects. The X500 model has its NavSat sensor removed and four PS05 sensors added; an evaluation-only OdometryPublisher provides ground truth on `/sim/truth/odom`.

## 9. ROS 2 architecture
17 packages (16 ament_python + interfaces); every node uses sim time; configuration from `configs/*.yaml` with per-scenario overrides; JSON status topics for observability.

## 10. Sensor architecture
Forward RGB 640×480 @ 10 Hz (80°), 3D LiDAR 360×16 @ 10 Hz (±25°, 30 m), downward RGB 640×480 @ 15 Hz (60°), downward 32×32 flash LiDAR (70°×70°). Details: `docs/SENSOR_FUSION.md`.

## 11. Camera processing
`camera_processor` validates encoding/size/timestamps/CameraInfo, publishes health and applies scenario fault injection (blur, exposure, noise, timestamp offset, occlusion, blackout).

## 12. LiDAR processing
`lidar_processor`: finite/range/self filtering (0.6 m main, 0.35 m downward — the latter removes landing-gear returns), health, fault injection (Gaussian range noise, dropout, blackout).

## 13. TF2 architecture
world → map → odom → base_link → {camera, lidar, down_camera, down_lidar} links and REP-103 optical frames. Static mounts from `configs/sensors.yaml` (also used to generate the SDF; a unit test checks they agree); odom → base_link from EKF2. Runtime TF validation in `scripts/check_system.py`.

## 14. Timestamp synchronisation
Explicit nearest-neighbour pairing of each LiDAR scan with a camera frame, rejecting |Δt| > 50 ms; accepted/rejected counts and |Δt| statistics published and logged.

## 15. Sensor fusion
P_cam = T_cam_lidar·P_lidar (TF2 at the scan stamp), u = fx·X/Z + cx, v = fy·Y/Z + cy with the live CameraInfo; only in-image, in-front points are coloured; output `/fused/points` (x, y, z, rgb, in_fov). Projection-error metrics: extrinsic shift (px) and LiDAR-silhouette ↔ image-edge chamfer (px).

## 16. 3D mapping
Bounded 200×200×50 log-odds voxel map at 0.25 m with ray tracing (free space along each beam), FREE/UNKNOWN/OCCUPIED, fused RGB per voxel; degraded LiDAR-only mode if the fused stream stalls.

## 17. Obstacle inflation
Planning radius 1.20 m = vehicle 0.40 + localisation 0.15 + control 0.15 + clearance 0.25 + half planning cell 0.25 (`configs/safety.yaml`); live LiDAR hard envelope 0.70 m, kept below the planner's guaranteed surface clearance (0.77 m).

## 18. Approved mission corridor
Mission box x, y ∈ [1, 49] m, z ∈ [1, 10] m intersected with a 12 m tube around the approved centreline, minus a 0.5 m margin; A* cannot leave it and every trajectory is re-validated against it. PS05 spatial error E vs Emax = 2.0 m monitored in flight with alarm and containment.

## 19. 3D A*
26-connected weighted A* (w = 1.3, no corner cutting, optimistic unknown at 1.2× cost), line-of-sight pruning, verified Chaikin smoothing, trapezoidal speed profile (2 m/s, 1 m/s², 1 m/s vertical), single 2 cm validity check for pruning, smoothing and final validation. `docs/PLANNING.md`.

## 20. Local replanning
Look-ahead 8 m checked against every LiDAR scan and every map update; blocked → OBSTACLE_STOP (hover) → REPLANNING from the current pose inside the same corridor → NAVIGATE; no route → NO_SAFE_PATH (hover + 3 retries) → ABORTED.

## 21. GPS-denied design
No GNSS sensor on the airframe, GPS fusion disabled, external tracking (60 Hz, 10 ms latency, σ_r = 5 cm, σ_θ = σ_φ = 1.5 mrad) converted with the PS05 equations and fused by EKF2. Truth is evaluation-only; a bring-up finding (PX4 gz_bridge re-publishing the evaluation odometry as external vision) was fixed and is now guarded by static and runtime audit checks.

## 22. Landing target detection
AprilTag 36h11 (OpenCV ArUco), sub-pixel corners, IPPE-square PnP, TF2 to map, exponential filter; the marker is used only after GPS-free navigation reached the approximate landing zone.

## 23. LiDAR landing validation
Plane fit on the lowest returns in a 1.2 m disc around the tag: tilt ≤ 8°, RMS ≤ 5 cm, no returns > 0.15 m above the plane within 2.0 m, alignment ≤ 0.35 m. A marker alone never triggers descent.

## 24. Precision landing controller
PID per axis on the map-frame tag error (Kp 0.8, Ki 0.05, Kd 0.15, 0.6 m/s limit, clamped and conditional integration, filtered derivative); descent 0.4 → 0.25 m/s with re-validation at 2.0 / 1.0 / 0.5 m; blind-descent zone below 1.0 m; PX4 LAND at 0.45 m AGL.

## 25. Safety state machine
INIT → ARMING → TAKEOFF → PLANNING → NAVIGATE → LANDING_ZONE_SEARCH → TARGET_LOCK → ALIGN → DESCEND → FINAL_CHECK → LAND → LANDED, with OBSTACLE_STOP, REPLANNING, NO_SAFE_PATH, TARGET_LOST, UNSAFE_PAD, ABORT_CLIMB, RETURN_HOME, SENSOR_FAILURE, CORRIDOR_BREACH, ABORTED. Pure-Python, unit-tested against a kinematic vehicle for every branch. `docs/LANDING.md`.

## 26. Backend architecture
FastAPI: REST endpoints for health, system, mission, vehicle, sensors, map, planner, landing, metrics (current + history), experiments (list/detail/start/stop), scenarios, logs; WebSocket `/ws/telemetry`; pydantic validation, CORS, structured logging; fed by the read-only `dashboard_bridge`.

## 27. Frontend / dashboard
React + TypeScript + Vite + Tailwind + three.js: GPS/autonomy/simulation status, state-machine strip with failure states, forward and downward camera feeds (tag overlay), interactive 3D view (obstacles, occupancy voxels, fused cloud, corridor, planned/local/actual paths, target), vehicle status and PS05 E-vs-Emax gauge, live metrics, telemetry charts, sensor health, landing checklist, event timeline and experiment control/history. Only live or recorded data is displayed.

## 30. Metrics
Landing error E = √((Px−Tx)²+(Py−Ty)²) at PX4-detected touchdown (truth) vs. pad centre; localisation error = |EKF estimate − truth|; true spatial error = |truth − trajectory reference| during NAVIGATE (PS05 E); minimum clearance = distance from the vehicle centre to the nearest obstacle surface (truth geometry); collision = clearance < vehicle radius 0.40 m; near miss = clearance < 0.65 m; planning / replanning latency = planner service time; detection latency = unexpected-obstacle placement → first detection; map accuracy = occupied voxels farther than 0.5 m from any true surface (phantoms).

## 32. Robustness tests
NOT MEASURED

## 33. Failure modes
Failure modes found and fixed during bring-up (ground truth leaking into EKF2 through PX4's gz_bridge, uXRCE timesync vs. sim time, home latched before EKF convergence, gpu_lidar cube-map seam phantoms, landing-gear self-returns, tag too small / too large for the camera, A* corner cutting, inconsistent validation sampling, landing in place after an unsafe-pad abort) are listed with root causes in `docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md`. Injected failures (LiDAR/camera blackout, timestamp offset, tag loss, unsafe pad, no path, extrinsic error, sensor noise) and their measured outcomes are in section 32.

## 34. Limitations
* Localisation uses a *simulated* external tracking station (as PS05 prescribes); its noise model is Gaussian and line-of-sight occlusion of the tracker is not modelled. On-board GPS-free odometry (VIO / LiDAR odometry) is not implemented.
* All results are simulation-only (Gazebo Harmonic, lockstep PX4 SITL) on one world; no hardware or field data.
* Under load the simulator runs below real time and the forward camera renders below its 10 Hz target, so a fraction of LiDAR scans has no camera frame within the 50 ms sync window (those scans are mapped without colour). Python nodes bound the achievable rates.
* The planner treats unknown space optimistically; newly observed obstacles cause stop-and-replan cycles (safe but slower than a continuously re-optimising local planner).
* Weighted A* (w = 1.3) trades bounded sub-optimality for speed.
* The landing tag pose z is biased by ~0.2–0.3 m (texture scale); only the horizontal tag position is used and height comes from the downward LiDAR.

## 35. Future work
On-board LiDAR-inertial odometry as a second, independent localisation source with tracker-loss handling; continuous local trajectory optimisation (e.g. MPC / kinodynamic search) instead of stop-and-replan; C++ ports of mapping and planning; nested AprilTags for continuous visual guidance to touchdown; wind and sensor-latency stress tests; hardware-in-the-loop and field trials with the PS05 ground tracker.

## 36. Reproducibility
Version-locked Docker image (`docs/ENVIRONMENT.md`); world and vehicle generated from versioned YAML; every run stores its scenario, seed, full configuration, config hash and git revision. Commands: `./scripts/run_tests.sh`, `./scripts/smoke_test.sh`, `./scripts/run_full_campaign.sh 20 10 1`, `python3 scripts/aggregate_results.py`, `python3 scripts/generate_report.py`.

## 37. Conclusion
The system demonstrates, in simulation and with logged evidence, GPS-independent 3D navigation inside an approved corridor, LiDAR–camera fusion and 3D mapping, replanning around unexpected obstacles, and LiDAR-validated precision landing, together with explicit safe behaviour for every injected failure. The measured results above — not design targets — are the basis for any claim made from this work.
